patterns.message: Import across projects by package name (@cadastre/x), never by a relative path: a relative path escaping its project is invisible to the boundary rules below, which match on package names (ADR-0006).

A context (type:context) and the edge (type:edge) may depend only on the published language (@cadastre/api-contracts), the shared kernel (@cadastre/shared) and technical adapters (@cadastre/event-publisher). The way out is the contracts package: route cross-context traffic through it, never through another context's internals (ADR-0006).
Import across projects by package name (@cadastre/x), never by a relative path: a relative path escaping its project is invisible to the boundary rules below, which match on package names (ADR-0006).

Contracts (type:contracts) and technical adapters (type:adapter) may depend only on the shared kernel (@cadastre/shared). The way out is to move what you need into the kernel if its meaning is identical everywhere, or to leave it with its owner if it is not (ADR-0006).
Import across projects by package name (@cadastre/x), never by a relative path: a relative path escaping its project is invisible to the boundary rules below, which match on package names (ADR-0006).

The shared kernel (type:kernel) is the bottom of the stack and depends on nothing in the workspace. The way out is to leave the concept with the context that owns it: if only one context needs it, it is not kernel (ADR-0006).
